Inside the box, from top to bottom, it sequentially contains the black GATE (metal gate), Silicon Dioxide (silicon dioxide), Si (silicon body region), and the black BODY contact. The dashed box does not only enclose a certain layer, but encloses the whole of these material parts. Reasoning: The problem states that the initial state is uncharged, therefore the initial total charge of the entire structure inside the dashed box is 0. After applying a +3 V gate-body bias, the measured charge inside the silicon dioxide layer is +Q. Since the dashed box contains the entire MOS structure, the bias will only cause charge separation or redistribution between different regions inside the box; total charge is conserved, so the remaining parts inside the box other than silicon dioxide must together carry -Q. Thus the total charge inside the dashed box is +Q + (-Q) = 0. Therefore the magnitude of the total charge expressed in units of Q is 0.

method.method_draft: First identify the dashed box as enclosing all material parts of the MOS structure shown. From the text, note that the structure starts uncharged and that after the +3 V gate-to-body bias the silicon dioxide contains +Q. Since the entire device inside the dashed box was initially neutral, the bias can only separate or redistribute charges between included regions. Therefore the rest of the enclosed structure carries total charge -Q, making the total charge inside the dashed box +Q - Q = 0. Expressed as a multiple of Q, the answer is 0.
